jcr:title: Surgicount-Triton
jcr:description: Together, let's help put an end to retained surgical sponges.

largeheadline.line2: Our goal is zero retained surgical sponges and maternal harm

text.text: Designed to help nurses prevent retained surgical sponges and assess real-time blood loss across the continuum of care. With the latest generation of SurgiCount+, you can digitize your facility's hemorrhage protocol, standardize the QBL process, and feel confident in your surgical sponge count and blood loss assessment.

text_654000976.text: There are 50,000 cases of severe maternal morbidity annually nationwide¹

text_copy.text: 88% of retained surgical items are due to a false correct count²

text.text: 70% of pregnancy-related deaths from hemorrhage are preventable⁴

Learn how it works

Learn more about the features and benefits of SurgiCount+, now integrated with Triton technology.

SurgiCount – a sponge management solution that helps save time by standardizing your clinical protocol for charting sponge use.

Triton – Assess real-time cumulative blood loss across the continuum of care, integrating hospital-specific protocols and text alerts to help coordinate the clinical team’s hemorrhage response.

largeheadline_copy.line1:
SurgiCount+ and Triton 
Trusted solution. Standardized care.

text_copy_copy.text:
A) Sponge management solution
Helps save time by standardizing your clinical protocol for charting sponge use.

B) Universal reporting tool
Leveraging the URT analytics dashboard provides visibility to hospital-wide trends and drives data-based decision making, standardization, and continuous quality improvements.

C) Real time EMR integration
Track and communicate patient information with one seamless workflow.

D) Bluetooth enabled Reader
Count, track, and locate surgical sponges within the operating room and sterile fields. 

E) Triton AI 
Assess real-time cumulative blood loss across the continuum of care and differentiate blood from other fluids. 

F) Triton QBL
Integrate hospital-specific protocols and text alerts to help coordinate the clinical team's hemorrhage response.
